goal: A 90-second vertical cut of the interview with the dead air and the ums gone, captions on, the best 90 seconds of what was said.
audience: a phone viewer scrolling a feed
assumptions: captions burned in the studio's caption design, not default subtitles
captions are word-accurate, burned in, plus an SRT file
the 90 s is reached by cutting — selecting the best material, never padding
the human's file is read-only: never modified, moved or deleted
dialog audio stays clear: one mix at the loudness target
the cut is made from the human's interview file ~/Videos/i.mp4 (read-only, sha-pinned)
the source is referenced read-only: path + sha256 recorded in inputs.json

decision.why: The ask is a cut of real footage with measured trims: the ums come out by the filler cut (verified against the audio), the pacing by the silence map, the captions from the transcript — the edit technique is built for exactly this.

alternatives.rejected_because: a code-drawn piece cannot use the real footage — the ask is the interview itself

alternatives.id: simplest: one hard trim to the first 90 seconds
alternatives.rejected_because: the simplest thing that could work, but it ignores 'no ums' and the content: the best 90 seconds are rarely the first

segments.brief: Ingest the interview, transcribe, cut the fillers and the dead air (every proposal vetoed by its removed text), arrange the best 90 seconds, caption it, reframe if the source is widescreen.
acceptance: no ums survive (the filler cut's proposals applied)
the piece contains only real footage from i.mp4 (no stock, no synthetic inserts)
the clip reads as one coherent interview excerpt
'no ums': filler words (um, uh, you know) are removed, verified against the audio
9:16 vertical: the framing keeps the speaker composed (a reframe, not a center crop)
'no ums': the filler words (um, uh, you know) are removed
captions: word-accurate, burned in, plus SRT
captions word-accurate, burned-in, plus SRT from the same transcript
clean in/out points, no mid-word cuts

blocked_inputs: input:i1 — ~/Videos/i.mp4 does not exist (the human must point at the real file)

risks: the source may be much longer than 90s of good material
